item.title: Crime Rates Suggest Detroit Is Safer. But Youth Still Live in Fear.
item.description: “I didn’t feel safe anywhere": Harassment, violence and unsafe commutes shape daily life for teens, who remain on high alert.

item.title: The Many Faces of North Philadelphia
item.description: From jazz shows and art installations to neighborhood memories and sound systems on wheels, the first North Philadelphia History Festival celebrated the legacy and continued evolution of one of the city’s most storied communities.

item.title: Linking City and Countryside To Solve Food Insecurity
item.description: In Kentucky’s dense cities and smallest towns, nonprofits are bridging the gap between those who grow food, those who have excess and those who need it.

item.title: Slowly But Surely, Foundations Are Changing How They Invest Their Endowments
item.description: As grantees ask hard questions about where their grant money comes from, more and more foundations are putting their endowments in the hands of asset management firms focused on investments that align with their grantmaking.

item.title: What It Takes To Keep Kentucky’s Black-Led Farms Alive
item.description: As federal support is cut and public conservation efforts fall short in reaching rural Black farmers, one Black-led organization is creating new lifelines to protect historic legacies.

item.title: Checkpoint 300 and the Architecture of Control
item.description: Mark Griffiths shows how the infamous Checkpoint 300 embodies larger geographies of Israeli control — reshaping a once-vibrant commercial strip in the West Bank.

item.title: Next City’s 2025 Gift Guide: The Best Gifts for Urbanists, City Planners & Community Advocates
item.description: Meaningful gift ideas for the people working to improve our cities.

item.title: A Community Land Trust Is Raising the Bar for Community Power in Economic Development
item.description: Denver’s Tierra Colectiva is showing how residents can shape — and own — mixed-use projects at a scale once reserved for private developers.

item.title: This Bronx Project Is Setting a New Standard for Community-Controlled Development
item.description: After decades of failed mega-projects, the Kingsbridge Armory is now the site of one of the country’s most ambitious experiments in community ownership and shared control.

item.title: Residents Halted Development on a Historic Burial Ground. Now They Want a Say in What Comes Next.
item.description: Flatbush residents want a collaborative memorial process. Instead, they say the city is moving ahead with little transparency and even less community input.
